pages.title: Base Cost and Complexity
pages.text: Each cast costs:$(br2)F=5+10*C+0.625*C^2$(br2)5 is the fixed startup cost; C is total structural complexity. An entity effect contributes 0.1 and a modifier 0.05. Combine complexity before converting to focus once. Damage values and actual target counts do not change C.

pages.title: Simple and Complex Spells
pages.text: Using the same self selector and damage effects:$(br2)1 effect: C=0.3, about 8.06 focus.$(br)10 effects: C=1.2, 17.90 focus.$(br)50 effects: C=5.2, 73.90 focus.$(br2)More complex structures carry an increasing burden. Raising one damage value only increases aether.

pages.title: Loops
pages.text: Let C be body complexity and n the maximum repetitions. Loop complexity is:$(br2)0.2 + L(n)*C$(br2)L(n)=log2(1+n). For C=0.3 and n=10, loop complexity is about 1.238; combine it with the rest of the structure before calculating focus. Aether still counts every effect.

pages.title: Delays
pages.text: A delay adds 0.15+H(t) complexity, plus its action.$(br2)H(t)=0.05*log2(1+t/20), with t in ticks. Normally 20 ticks make a second. Repeated delays use the span from first to last repetition, rather than charging focus each tick.

pages.title: Branches
pages.text: Branch complexity is:$(br2)0.1+P+max(A,B)+0.25*min(A,B)$(br2)P is condition complexity; A and B are branch complexities. Preparing a fallback adds a small burden. Aether pays for the chosen branch, but reserves for the more expensive one.

pages.title: Damage Prices
pages.text: Ordinary damage costs, per target and attempt:$(br2)m(d)=500*d+12.5*d*d$(br2)Damage 4 costs 2.2K aether; 20 costs 15K; 100 costs 175000. Stronger single hits cost more per damage point. Damage types share the default price. Focus does not grow with d.

pages.title: Symbols in Effect Entries
pages.text: d: requested damage; v: speed; r: teleport distance; t: ticks; a: amplifier, where zero means level I; k: price factor, default 1.$(br2)Timed effects start at 20*t*(a+1)^2*k. Instant effects use 1K*(a+1)^2*k. Trust the actual readings on your core.

pages.title: Selections and Limits
pages.text: Each selection affects at most 8 targets by default, nearest to its origin first. Reserves cover all 8 slots; settlement normally pays only for actual targets; a complete miss also loses part of the unused reserve.$(br2)Repetitions, range, lifetime and simultaneous casts also have limits. Unbounded costs or excessive settings prevent casting. Reduce the range or repetitions.

pages.title: Base Costs on Cores
pages.text: Core tooltips calculate base aether and focus from saved values, including local variables, loop indices, repetition counts, areas and effect levels.$(br2)Base prices assume one target and multipliers of 1. Additional targets, travel distance and future random values are not part of the fixed base.
